status_summary: On or before 2025-03-21 DHS began reductions in force at the Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties (CRCL), the Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman (OIDO) and the CIS Ombudsman (CISOMB). Three nonprofits sued on 2025-04-24 (RFK Human Rights v. DHS, D.D.C. No. 1:25-cv-01270); on 2025-05-23 the court denied a temporary restraining order without prejudice and ordered DHS to post notices that the three offices remained open, and a DHS declaration of 2025-05-22 had projected much smaller staffs (roughly 20 casework staff for CRCL and 5 to 7 each for the ombudsman offices, against about 140, 100 and 40 before). A declaration by the CIS Ombudsman executed 2026-02-13 reports CRCL at 33 to 38 staff (mostly contractors, with two rehired federal employees), OIDO with three hires (two of them rehired) plus two attorneys, and CISOMB with the Ombudsman, a deputy and one detailee; it says administrative functions were realigned to the Management Directorate under the workforce optimization initiative, and that the offices are independent of the General Counsel and report to the Secretary. Plaintiffs' summary judgment motion was briefed from 2026-01-16 to 2026-02-27 and no ruling was found; none of the offices has been folded into the General Counsel or abolished.

timeline.event: Reports said DHS was carrying out reductions in force at CRCL, OIDO and CISOMB.
Three nonprofits sued DHS in the District of Columbia to restore the three offices (RFK Human Rights v. DHS, No. 1:25-cv-01270).
A DHS declaration outlined plans to keep the three offices open with much smaller staffs (CRCL about 20 casework staff plus leadership, each ombudsman 5 to 7), using detailees.

A declaration by the CIS Ombudsman, also acting as deputy for CRCL and OIDO, reported CRCL at 33 to 38 staff with two rehired federal employees, OIDO with three hires including two rehired employees, and CISOMB with three people; it said human resources, contracting, finance and IT functions were realigned to the Management Directorate and that the offices report to the Secretary, not the General Counsel.
